analysis.title: Global Markets Daily: The Factors Behind the Rise in US Yields
key_insights: US Treasury yields have risen across the curve. Front-end pricing is hawkish relative to GS economists' Fed baseline, and longer-term forwards are 40-to-50bp above fair value.
The selloff came in phases: a lower vol regime through much of the summer, then a higher vol selloff more recently.

The shift in expected policy path from cuts to hikes, amid higher inflation risks and diminished labor market concerns since the eve of the US-Iran conflict, explains the bulk of the rise in longer-term UST yields (about 70% of the cumulative move).
10y Treasury yields are up over 100bp since the start of the year and 130bp since the year-to-date lows set on the eve of the US-Iran conflict.

Front-end and nearer-term forwards drove more of the point-to-point move since end-February, but forwards further out the curve drove the most recent phase of the selloff. Breakevens played a limited role and the real component drove the higher longer-term yields.

The selloff since late August came in two phases. The first spanned Jackson Hole and the September central bank decisions with bearish impulses from all major markets. The last three weeks have been almost exclusively US-driven, with Germany exporting bullish shocks amid greater stress in sovereign spreads.
5y5y UST yields are 5.5-5.6%, 40-to-50bp above GS's G10 framework fair value and close to one standard deviation cheap. The gap opened only after the break into the mid-5% range.

Consensus 1y-ahead short-term rate forecasts are up about 125bp this year, worth about 55bp to longer-term forwards. Higher longer-term growth expectations and foreign spillovers add another 10-to-15bp combined.

The US fiscal trajectory is not sustainable but has not meaningfully shifted this year, and privately held USTs as a share of GDP are about stable. What changed is expectations of AI-related spending and borrowing.

AI investment spending likely supports higher yields through longer-term growth optimism and cyclical resilience. Corporate debt issuance has a local effect on the day of pricing but a much weaker effect over longer windows, so GS finds little evidence that debt supply absorption is a significant source of upward pressure.
About 10-to-15bp of the year-to-date yield move is unexplained by fundamentals. The 10y residual is comparable, with the policy path worth 80-85bp.

At the front end the market prices a more hawkish Fed path than surveys. Higher vol and diminished hedge value (front-end rate and equity correlation) explain 25-to-30bp of the 40-to-50bp market-versus-survey gap. These factors also raise bond risk premium.
Bonds have been a poor diversifier for equities, partly because yields are strongly positively correlated with energy prices.
Bond funds' duration position relative to the Bloomberg Agg has moved steadily underweight, to levels that have historically seen yields skew lower over the following 3-to-6 months.

Negative convexity in MBS and Treasury futures amplified the selloff since early September. GS estimates about $60bn of 10y-equivalent paying needs from MBS hedgers (likely the high side of realized flows) and $10-to-15bn of 10y-equivalent selling by asset managers to offset CTD-driven duration extension, though they sold significantly more.
MBS index-level convexity is now about zero and CTD-switch risk is no longer clearly asymmetric to higher yields, so convexity should be a much smaller factor in further selloffs.
Market stress measures look fairly orderly with little evidence of concentrated UST selling by global investors. Front-end swap spreads have tightened modestly since late August.

GS is more bullish on US duration: yields are elevated versus macro fundamentals, positioning is underweight and technical risks have diminished. Energy remains the main source of day-to-day rates vol, while recent credit spread widening provides a brake on higher yields.
Holding current yield levels would raise the drag on growth from financial conditions from 0.2pp to more than 0.5pp.

GS's fundamental view is that underlying inflation pressures are contained, so front-end pricing is too hawkish and there is excess risk premium across the US curve. A credible reduction in energy risks, weaker growth news or diminished confidence in the AI trade would likely take yields sharply lower. Absent those, an accumulation of benign inflation news may take a few months to build the case for longs.

risk_factors: Energy risks remain unresolved and growth risks stay low, which would push 10y yields above the 4.75% year-end forecast.
Energy price swings continue to drive day-to-day rates volatility and the positive yield-energy correlation weakens bonds as an equity diversifier.
Higher macro uncertainty and weaker diversification value raise bond risk premium.
Confidence in the AI trade, hyperscaler capex and borrowing expectations feed longer-term growth optimism and yields.
About 10-to-15bp of the year-to-date yield rise is unexplained by GS's macro framework.
Sovereign spread stress in Germany and foreign spillovers can move US yields.
Possible foreign official sales of USTs accompanying dollar strength.
charts_described: Exhibit 3 plots the 5y5y UST yield against model-implied fair value, with yields recently 40-to-50bp above fair value.
Exhibit 8 shows the US Fund Positioning Indicator at a current score of -2, indicating bearish sentiment on duration.
Exhibit 9 shows Bloomberg US MBS index-level convexity at about zero following the most recent duration extension.
vol_and_positioning: Rates vol is elevated, with 1y10y implied vol jumping and term premium rising. GS sees elevated rate vol as making it attractive to sell the tail to significantly higher yields to start adding long exposure, either standalone or via risk-reversals.
Higher vol and the lower hedge value of rates versus equities explain about 25-to-30bp of the 40-to-50bp front-end market-versus-survey gap.
US Fund Positioning Indicator at -2 (bearish sentiment), consistent with bond funds underweight duration versus the Bloomberg Agg.
MBS index-level convexity is about zero after the most recent duration extension, and CTD-switch risk is no longer clearly asymmetric to higher yields.
Yields are firmly above model fair value while bond funds are clearly underweight duration, a combination GS calls unusual.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict and the associated energy price shock shifted policy expectations from cuts to hikes and keep energy a main source of day-to-day rates volatility.
Greater stress in sovereign spreads in Germany has made it an exporter of bullish shocks onto global duration.

tension_points.bull_case: Yields are elevated versus macro fundamentals, bond funds are underweight duration, convexity technicals have faded and credit spread widening acts as a brake. Underlying inflation is contained, so front-end pricing is too hawkish and the curve carries excess risk premium.
tension_points.bear_case: Upside risks to the 4.75% year-end 10y forecast remain if energy risks are unresolved and growth risks stay low. Valuation arguments for lower yields have been challenged and the case for longs may take a few months of benign inflation news.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy risks stay unresolved and growth risks stay low, pushing yields above the 4.75% year-end forecast.
